decisions.reason: Define-XML ADQSCIBC.EFFFL names ADSL.FASFL, which is absent from retained ADSL; the implemented ADSL.EFFFL is a differently named source.

ADQSCIBC.AVISITN explicitly directs windowing on ADY, and the literal probe applies the native SAP page-11 intervals and documented numeric codes faithfully. Its donor-day versus recipient-visit differences remain, and the added SAP date-subtraction reading also fails to reproduce the reference; SAP page-15 supplies recipient visits without a complete retained-date override.

ADQSCIBC.AVAL states the direct CIBIC QS.QSSTRESN rule implemented by the literal probe, which differs on the reported imputed records. Data guide pages 6-7 and SAP pages 10-11 justify the separate targeted-LOCF reading, which reproduces the reference without copying the current AVAL.

ADQSCIBC.STUDYID and data guide page-4 name ADSL, while the global derivation obtains STUDYID from QS for obs and both grouped LOCF templates. The keyed ADSL input does not supply the column through an intermediate.
ADQSCIBC.USUBJID and data guide page-4 name ADSL, but the global and grouped row paths obtain USUBJID from QS. No intervening derivation returns ADSL.USUBJID.

SAP page-11 restricts the final window to days above 140, while obs assigns Week 24 by an unconditional otherwise branch, including missing ADY. The native baseline cell is <=1; its omitted underline is not the basis for this difference.

The AVISIT-to-AVISITN path inherits obs window conditions that lack the SAP page-11 lower Week 8 bound and explicit final day>140 condition. In particular, missing ADY receives the final visit code rather than having an eligible assessment-day window.

ADQSCIBC.VISIT names QS.VISIT, which obs copies directly and both LOCF templates obtain through _SRC_VISIT and DONOR16 or DONOR24 from SELF observations. All transitive source paths therefore resolve to the documented QS variable.

The obs rule reads QS.VISITNUM and both LOCF templates carry it through DONOR16 or DONOR24 and _SRC_VISITNUM. These intermediates retain the source named in ADQSCIBC.VISITNUM; a separate donor-selection policy does not erase that source.

SAP page-11 specifies unshifted days from randomization, whereas ADQSCIBC.ADY and the consumed study_day operation use TRTSDT and add one on or after that date. Even the shared visit-3 source does not equate those arithmetic conventions.
SAP page-11 selects the prior assessment for an equidistant pair. The ascending AWTARGET-ADY secondary sort in obs instead puts the later assessment first.

SAP page-10 specifies imputation of missing efficacy values, while locf16 treats any DONOR16 record at the target visit as a hit without checking its score. The same record-presence mechanism in locf24 can suppress a missing-score recipient.

SAP page-15 calls the Week 8 summary LOCF, but lists Week 8 as the first CIBIC+ assessment visit, leaving no earlier scheduled CIBIC+ target score to carry. The summary instruction does not require an additional Week 8 dataset row without an eligible predecessor, and obs already provides the observed Week 8 scores.

The SAP page-18 Week 8 LOCF table title is read with the postbaseline CIBIC+ visit list on page-15 and the targeted-assessment donor restriction on pages 10-11. It does not independently prescribe a synthetic first-visit recipient when no earlier targeted CIBIC+ score exists.

SAP page-15 defines CIBIC+ visits as Weeks 8, 16 and 24, and page-46 defines a change assessment rather than a baseline score. The baseline row shared with ADAS-Cog on page-11 does not establish a CIBIC+ baseline record requiring an executable AWTARGET branch.

ADQSCIBC.ADT and native QS.QSDTC state date conversion and its SV visit source, but do not state first-day completion of partial dates. The data guide page-5 first-of-month rule applies to adverse events.

SAP pages 10-11 and data guide page-6 specify selected targeted score candidates but do not prescribe descending QSSEQ as a final SCORE16 donor tiebreak. No CIBIC+ native value-level rule adds that policy.

ADQSCIBC.ANL01FL, its Y_BLANK codelist and data guide page-6 distinguish selected Y records from unselected records. Empty-string output for the latter is the ordinary blank character representation, not another selection condition or computation.

SAP page-11 resolves opposite-side equidistant assessments but does not break repeated assessments on the same closest day. ADQSCIBC.ANL01FL and data guide page-6 also do not fully assign every added recipient flag, leaving a real selection gap even after native visit-date sources and routine blank encoding are considered.

ADQSCIBC.DTYPE and data guide page-7 reserve LOCF for records whose values were imputed by that method. Leaving ordinary observed rows blank is the character representation of no imputation type, not a new clinical derivation condition.

SAP pages 10-11 and data guide pages 6-7 identify targeted score donors but do not define the separate unrestricted DONOR16 metadata role. Its filter also determines target-record presence, an operational selection not supplied by the sequence traceability statement.

The retained CIBIC+ LOCF and traceability statements on data guide pages 6-7 and SAP pages 10-11 do not prescribe descending QSSEQ for DONOR24 metadata ties. ADQSCIBC.QSSEQ is an ordinary source comment without a LOCF-specific value-level selection method.

ADQSCIBC.DTYPE and data guide page-7 define the imputation event, but SAP pages 10-11 do not complete added-recipient eligibility, residual donor ties or separate score-versus-metadata donor assignment. Those are actual operational gaps for reconstructing the implemented event, independent of blank serialization or the Week 8 summary title.

ADQSCIBC.AWRANGE and SAP page-11 state the postbaseline ranges for the CIBIC+ visits listed on page-15. Their ordinary string rendering and the shared baseline cell underline lost by extraction do not leave this interval rule without sources, conditions or computation.

ADQSCIBC.AWLO, its integer type and SAP page-11 determine starts at the finite postbaseline boundaries, including the first integer above 140. SAP page-15 supplies the CIBIC+ visit scope, so a hypothetical shared-baseline endpoint does not prevent a whole-variable probe.
SAP page-11 makes the Week 24 interval unbounded above. A missing numeric AWHI represents the absence of a finite endpoint and does not add an undocumented window condition or computation.

ADQSCIBC.AWHI and SAP page-11 give the finite postbaseline ends and no finite Week 24 end, with CIBIC+ scope supplied by page-15. Routine missing representation of the open endpoint does not make that rule incomplete.

ADQSCIBC.QSSEQ names QS.QSSEQ and data guide page-7 provides traceability, but neither prescribes DONOR16 as a separate latest-observation sequence source unrestricted by ANL01FL. SAP pages 10-11 concern selected score donors and do not add this metadata ranking or its sequence tiebreak.

The source and traceability rules in ADQSCIBC.QSSEQ and data guide page-7 do not specify the DONOR24 analysis-visit, day and descending-sequence ranking. The native item has no LOCF value-level exception that would supply this independent metadata-donor choice.

Native ADQSCIBC.QSSEQ contains only the ordinary QS.QSSEQ source comment, and data guide page-7 identifies the traceability key rather than the added-row sequence donor. SAP pages 10-11 specify score candidates without deciding whether the recipient sequence follows that score donor or a separate observation, so a lookup using the existing target QSSEQ cannot independently derive it.

Define-XML ADQSCIBC.AVISITN explicitly applies SAP windows to ADY, whose definition adds one on or after TRTSDT, while SAP page-11 uses plain date subtraction. SAP page-9 and ADSL.TRTSDT identify the common Visit-3 anchor, so the window-day definitions still disagree on and after that date.

SAP page-11 defines the window input by plain visit-date minus randomization-date subtraction, whereas adqscibc.yaml obs lines 643-661 windows study_day and maps its label to AVISITN. ADQSCIBC.ADY explicitly adds one on or after TRTSDT; the common Visit-3 anchor does not remove that arithmetic difference.

missed.quote:
The datasets include only subjects who were enrolled in the study. Subjects who failed screening 
criteria were not included in analysis datasets.
missed.reason: The enrolled-subject restriction governs the observed row population and the subjects eligible for its added LOCF rows, but no claim cites this record-selection statement.

missed.quote: It contains one record per subject per VISIT.
missed.reason: This CIBIC+ source-record granularity statement is not cited by a claim and is distinct from the analysis-window assignment clauses.
